prompts.title: The Fourteenth Revision Request
prompts.prompt: Your client has asked for the logo to be bigger for the fourteenth time. Write five pairs of sentences about that thread. Each pair is one long sentence carrying the whole scene, then one short line that lands on it.
prompts.constraint: Exactly five pairs. The long sentence is 25 to 35 words. The short line is 3 to 6 words. The short line may not describe anything in the long sentence. It must judge, negate, ask a question, or name what it cost you.
prompts.check: Count the words. All five long sentences fall between 25 and 35, all five short lines fall between 3 and 6, and no short line contains an adjective.

prompts.title: Premium Without The Word
prompts.prompt: A founder selling a 28,000 rupee skincare kit wants the hero section to feel expensive. Write four hero blocks. Each block is one 25 to 35 word sentence about what the buyer has already tried, then a 3 to 6 word line under it.
prompts.constraint: Four blocks. The short line never describes the product. It judges the alternative, names a cost, or asks the buyer a question. Banned in the short lines: premium, luxury, quality, best, amazing.
prompts.check: Every short line is 3 to 6 words, contains no product feature, and could be deleted without losing a single fact.

prompts.title: Twelve Forty In The Afternoon
prompts.prompt: You woke at 12:40pm again. Write six pairs about the hour after waking: the light in the room, the phone, the plate your mother left covered on the table.
prompts.constraint: Six pairs. Long sentence 25 to 35 words, short line 3 to 6 words. At least two short lines must be questions and at least two must name a cost. None may contain the words lazy, guilty, or discipline.
prompts.check: Six short lines, each 3 to 6 words, at least two ending in a question mark and at least two naming something specifically lost.

prompts.title: He Stopped Replying
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about the client who went quiet after you sent the final Framer link. Take it from the last friendly message to the day you stopped checking your inbox for his name.
prompts.constraint: Every paragraph ends on a 3 to 6 word line that follows a 25 to 35 word sentence. Minimum eight paragraphs. No paragraph may end on a sentence longer than six words.
prompts.check: Read only the last line of each paragraph, in order. All are 3 to 6 words, and the sequence alone reads as an argument.

prompts.title: Blue Line At Six
prompts.prompt: You are on the metro at 6pm with a laptop bag held against your chest. Write about the seven minutes between two stations you actually use.
prompts.constraint: Under 150 words. Exactly four verdict beats: four sentences of 25 to 35 words, each followed by a line of 3 to 6 words. Nothing else in the piece.
prompts.check: The piece is exactly eight sentences. The odd-numbered ones are 25 to 35 words, the even-numbered ones are 3 to 6, and no even sentence describes anything.

prompts.title: Three Tiers, Three Beats
prompts.prompt: Write the pricing section for your own agency with three tiers. Under each tier put one long sentence about who it is for and one short line under that.
prompts.constraint: One 25 to 35 word sentence and one 3 to 6 word line per tier. The short lines must escalate in this order: the first names a cost, the second negates something, the third asks a question.
prompts.check: Three short lines of 3 to 6 words in the required order of cost, negation, question, and none of them lists a feature.

prompts.title: The Month Money Arrived
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about the first month you crossed one lakh. Include the exact evening you saw the number, who you told, who you did not tell, and what you bought that week.
prompts.constraint: Twelve verdict beats across the piece, spread so no two land in the same paragraph. Long sentence 25 to 35 words, short line 3 to 6 words. Ban the words finally, incredible, and unreal.
prompts.check: Twelve short lines of 3 to 6 words, none sharing a paragraph, and each one a judgement rather than a summary of the sentence before it.

prompts.title: Nine Days Without Japa
prompts.prompt: You did not sit for nine days. Write the record of it, day by day, with what took the hour instead. End on the day you sat again.
prompts.constraint: One verdict beat per day, nine in total. The long sentence carries the day and the excuse. The short line judges only you, never the practice, never the Guru, never the mantra.
prompts.check: Nine short lines of 3 to 6 words, all with you as the subject or implied subject, and none mentioning the practice itself.

prompts.title: His Homework At Midnight
prompts.prompt: Your younger brother walks in at 12:15am with a maths sheet. Write about what you did with the next twenty minutes.
prompts.constraint: Under 150 words. Exactly three verdict beats. The last short line must be the last line of the piece. No dialogue tags anywhere.
prompts.check: Three long sentences of 25 to 35 words, three short lines of 3 to 6 words, and the final line of the piece is one of the short ones.

prompts.title: Forty Thousand Rupees
prompts.prompt: Write 1,100 words about losing a client over an unpaid invoice. Cover the scope creep, the message you drafted three times, and the version you actually sent.
prompts.constraint: Fifteen verdict beats. Five must judge, five must negate, five must name a cost, and none may ask a question. Label them nowhere in the text, then list all fifteen by number at the bottom in their three groups.
prompts.check: The list at the bottom has fifteen entries in three groups of five, and each quoted line is 3 to 6 words and appears verbatim in the essay.

prompts.title: Long Page, Short Verdicts
prompts.prompt: Write a 1,000 word sales page for a landing page audit you sell. Use five sections: who it is for, what breaks, what you do, what it costs, what happens after.
prompts.constraint: Each section opens with a 25 to 35 word sentence and closes with a 3 to 6 word line. The five closing lines, read together with no other text, must form a complete argument for buying.
prompts.check: Copy the five closing lines into a separate block. Each is 3 to 6 words, and the block on its own persuades a stranger without the page around it.

prompts.title: A Year Of Nights
prompts.prompt: Write 1,000 words about a year of starting work at 10pm. Use one real week as the spine and let the whole year sit inside it.
prompts.constraint: Twenty verdict beats. No two consecutive short lines may use the same verb form, and no word may appear in more than one short line apart from articles and prepositions.
prompts.check: Twenty short lines, all 3 to 6 words, with zero repeated content words across the whole set.

prompts.title: Auto Layout For Ma
prompts.prompt: Explain to your mother what you actually did in Figma yesterday. She has never opened a design tool. Keep every real term you would use with a client.
prompts.constraint: Under 150 words. At least six unfamiliar terms, each given a 1 to 6 word plain gloss set off by commas right after the term. No parentheses, no which means, no in other words, no glossary at the end.
prompts.check: Six terms, six glosses, each gloss 1 to 6 words sitting between commas, and zero parentheses in the file.

prompts.title: Words The Buyer Skips
prompts.prompt: Write a 150 word section for a landing page whose buyers are clinic owners with no technical background. The product does compliant intake automation. Six pieces of jargon must survive into the copy.
prompts.constraint: Each of the six terms keeps its real name and carries a comma gloss of 1 to 6 words. You may not swap a term for a simpler word and you may not define one in a separate sentence.
prompts.check: Six terms present with their original spelling, each followed by a comma, a gloss of 1 to 6 words, and then a comma or a full stop.

prompts.title: Words From The Sitting
prompts.prompt: Write 140 words about this morning's practice for a friend who has never meditated. These terms must appear: japa, mala, ekagrata, asana, sankalpa, and one more you choose.
prompts.constraint: Each Sanskrit term takes a 1 to 6 word gloss between commas on first use only. Never gloss the same term twice. No parentheses and no italics doing the work of a definition.
prompts.check: Every Sanskrit term is glossed exactly once, on first appearance, in 1 to 6 words, and every later use runs bare.

prompts.title: Teaching Framer To A Friend
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words explaining to a school friend who sells clothes offline why you build in Framer instead of the tool you used before. Keep every real term you use at work.
prompts.constraint: Minimum fourteen glossed terms. Every gloss is 1 to 6 words, between commas, and uses no word of four or more syllables. Banned: parentheses, which means, that is, basically, essentially.
prompts.check: Fourteen or more comma glosses, none containing a word of four or more syllables, and no banned phrase anywhere in the file.

prompts.title: Kirana Store CRO
prompts.prompt: Explain conversion rate optimisation to the kirana store uncle downstairs, using his shop as the running example. Under 150 words.
prompts.constraint: Exactly eight glossed terms: conversion rate, bounce, funnel, split test, heatmap, above the fold, call to action, session. Each takes a 1 to 6 word gloss between commas. No parentheses.
prompts.check: All eight terms appear in the required form, each followed by a comma gloss of 1 to 6 words, and the piece stays under 150 words.

prompts.title: Above The Fold, Explained
prompts.prompt: Write the top 200 words of a landing page selling your Framer build service to founders whose only website was made on a drag and drop builder. They think a CMS is a person on your team. Keep every real term anyway.
prompts.constraint: Seven technical terms glossed inline. No gloss may use the words basically, simply, just, or essentially. The page must still read as sales copy rather than a tutorial.
prompts.check: Seven inline glosses of 1 to 6 words, zero instances of the four banned words, and no sentence starting with This means.

prompts.title: The Book I Cannot Explain
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about a chapter of Om Swami's memoir that stayed with you. Your reader thinks meditation is a phone app with rain sounds. Do not simplify a single term for them.
prompts.constraint: Twenty glossed terms minimum, mixing Sanskrit with design and business vocabulary. Every gloss is 1 to 6 words between commas and may not itself contain a Sanskrit word. No parentheses in the file.
prompts.check: Twenty or more comma glosses, all 1 to 6 words, every Sanskrit term glossed on first use, and zero parentheses.

prompts.title: Three Terms, Three Days
prompts.prompt: Pick three terms from your sadhana you have never had to say out loud to anyone: choose from purascharana, anushthana, bhava, siddhi, tapas, viveka. Write 600 words that use all three inside real situations from this week.
prompts.constraint: Each term appears at least three times. It gets a 1 to 6 word gloss on the first appearance only. No gloss may use another Sanskrit word.
prompts.check: Nine or more term appearances, exactly three glosses, all on first use, all 1 to 6 words, and none containing Sanskrit.

prompts.title: Six Glosses, Sixty Words
prompts.prompt: Describe the last hour of yesterday's client call in sixty words. The call contained six terms a stranger would not know.
prompts.constraint: Sixty words total, give or take three. Six glossed terms inside that budget. Every gloss 1 to 6 words, between commas.
prompts.check: Word count lands between 57 and 63, six comma glosses are present, and the piece still has a beginning and an end.

prompts.title: The Whole Craft, No Jargon
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words teaching a sharp fifteen year old how a landing page makes money. Write it for your brother. Keep every professional term you would use with a paying client.
prompts.constraint: Thirty glossed terms minimum. No term may be glossed twice. No gloss may exceed six words. No parentheses, no dashes, and no colons used to introduce a definition.
prompts.check: Thirty or more first-use comma glosses, zero repeats, zero parentheses, and zero colons introducing a definition.

prompts.title: Technical Page, Warm Read
prompts.prompt: Write a 1,000 word landing page for a headless commerce migration service sold to Indian D2C founders. They run their own store themselves and have never touched an API. The page still has to use the real words.
prompts.constraint: Twenty-five glossed terms, each 1 to 6 words between commas. The page must contain at least one price, one number of days, and one guarantee, and none of those three may be glossed.
prompts.check: Twenty-five comma glosses of 1 to 6 words, plus a price, a day count, and a guarantee that all appear unglossed.

prompts.title: Vocabulary Of A Bad Week
prompts.prompt: Write 1,000 words about the worst week of client work this year. Write it so your mother could read it end to end without stopping to ask you a single question.
prompts.constraint: Every term from work, money, health, or practice that she would not know gets one 1 to 6 word gloss on first use. Minimum twenty-two. No parentheses anywhere.
prompts.check: Highlight every noun a non-designer would not know. Each has a 1 to 6 word comma gloss on first use, twenty-two or more in total, and the file contains no parentheses.

prompts.title: Name The Thing
prompts.prompt: Write 120 words about the desk you are working at right now. Every object gets its actual name, brand, count, or material.
prompts.constraint: Zero category nouns. Banned: thing, stuff, item, object, furniture, equipment, device, setup, space. Minimum fifteen named nouns inside 120 words.
prompts.check: Fifteen or more nouns that name a make, a material, or a species, and none of the nine banned words appear.

prompts.title: Product Page, No Adjectives
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words of product copy for a brass diya set sold online during Diwali. Sell it without a single adjective.
prompts.constraint: No adjectives at all. Carry the sale on named materials, weights, measurements, and the things around the product: the windowsill, the marigold, the mustard oil, the cotton wick.
prompts.check: Zero adjectives in the file, and at least twelve concrete nouns naming a material, a measurement, or a species.

prompts.title: The Plate She Left
prompts.prompt: Write 130 words about the food waiting for you when you came out of your room at 1am. Nobody was awake. The plate had been covered for four hours.
prompts.constraint: Name every dish, vessel, and smell exactly. Banned words: food, meal, dinner, delicious, tasty, homemade, warm, nice.
prompts.check: At least five named dishes or ingredients, at least three named vessels, and none of the eight banned words.

prompts.title: One Room, Eight Hundred Words
prompts.prompt: Write 800 words about your working room between 11pm and 4am. Everything you feel has to be carried by what is physically in the room.
prompts.constraint: No emotion words at all. Banned: tired, lonely, happy, anxious, peaceful, motivated, and every word ending in -ness. Every abstraction gets swapped for a named physical thing.
prompts.check: Zero emotion words, zero -ness nouns, and every paragraph contains at least three nouns you could photograph.

prompts.title: Delhi At Forty-Six Degrees
prompts.prompt: Write 140 words about the walk from the metro gate to your building on a 46 degree afternoon. Six minutes, no shade, laptop bag on your back.
prompts.constraint: Ten named specifics minimum: the tree species, the vendor's exact goods, the surface underfoot, the sound, the drink, the brand of the drink. Banned: hot, heat, unbearable, scorching, boiling.
prompts.check: Ten or more named specifics including at least one plant species and one brand name, and none of the five banned words.

prompts.title: Ingredient, Not Benefit
prompts.prompt: Write 250 words of copy for a supplement sold to Indian women in their thirties. Use only ingredients, quantities, and physical outcomes.
prompts.constraint: No benefit language. Banned: support, boost, promote, wellness, balance, healthy, natural, gentle. Every claim must sit on a named ingredient with a milligram figure.
prompts.check: Zero banned words, and every sentence containing a claim also contains a named ingredient and a number with a unit.

prompts.title: Everything I Own
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about money without ever writing about money. Describe only the objects you have bought since you started earning, in the order you bought them.
prompts.constraint: The words money, rich, poor, expensive, cheap, afford, and success are banned. Each object gets a price, a month or date, and one physical detail nobody else would notice.
prompts.check: Every object carries three attached facts of price, time, and detail, and none of the seven banned words appear.

prompts.title: The Altar And The Desk
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words describing your practice without naming a single feeling or inner state. Only the objects, the timings, the sounds from the street, and your body.
prompts.constraint: Banned: peace, calm, bliss, divine, energy, vibration, presence, stillness, surrender. Every 100 words must contain one clock time and one named physical object.
prompts.check: All nine banned words absent, seven or more clock times present, and every 100 word block names an object you could hold.

prompts.title: Twelve Nouns, Three Days
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words about a fever that kept you in bed for three days. The room, the body, the medicine, and nothing else.
prompts.constraint: Exactly twelve nouns in the whole piece, all concrete, all visible in a photograph. Everything else must be verbs, and you may use no more than four adjectives.
prompts.check: Count the nouns. Exactly twelve, all photographable, and four or fewer adjectives in the file.

prompts.title: A City In Objects
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words about the neighbourhood you grew up in. Tell the whole thing through forty named things and nothing else.
prompts.constraint: Forty specific nouns, numbered in a list at the bottom to prove it. No generic category may appear anywhere: no shop, no vehicle, no tree, no snack, no building. Name the species, the brand, the model.
prompts.check: The list has forty entries, each appearing verbatim in the essay, and none of the five banned category words appears anywhere.

prompts.title: Full Page, Zero Abstractions
prompts.prompt: Write a 1,000 word landing page for a wedding photographer charging more than two lakh a day. His buyers are families who have already met four other photographers.
prompts.constraint: No abstract nouns anywhere. Ban the whole vocabulary of experience, memory, moment, journey, story, emotion, magic, and love. Sell with lenses, times of day, named rituals, weather, and counts.
prompts.check: Zero words from the banned abstraction list, and every section contains at least one named ritual, one time of day, and one count.

prompts.title: The Year In Fifty Objects
prompts.prompt: Write 1,000 words covering the last twelve months. Use fifty physical things as the only structure, one every two or three sentences.
prompts.constraint: Fifty named objects. No object repeats. No object may be a category. At least ten must carry a number: a price, a weight, a count, a temperature.
prompts.check: Fifty distinct named objects, zero repeats, zero categories, and ten or more carrying a number with a unit.

prompts.title: Kill Every Intensifier
prompts.prompt: Write 140 words about yesterday afternoon at your desk. Draft it however you like, then go back and delete every intensifier and put a number where each one stood.
prompts.constraint: Zero instances of very, really, so, extremely, incredibly, huge, tiny, tons, loads, forever, ages, a lot. Every deletion is replaced by a specific number, and at least four of those numbers must be uneven, like 41 minutes or 2,340 rupees.
prompts.check: Search the file for the twelve banned words. Zero hits, a number sits in every place one would have gone, and four or more of those numbers do not end in a zero.

prompts.title: Numbers Instead Of Very
prompts.prompt: Rewrite the hero line and subhead of your own agency page six times. Say what you do with counts, days, and rupees instead of degree words.
prompts.constraint: Six versions. Each contains at least three numbers and zero adjectives of degree. In each version at least two of the three numbers must be uneven.
prompts.check: Six pairs, eighteen or more numbers in total, twelve or more of them not round, and no degree adjectives anywhere.

prompts.title: How Tired, Exactly
prompts.prompt: You slept five hours and twelve minutes and your recovery score says 34 percent. Write 130 words about the day that followed without using a single word for how it felt.
prompts.constraint: Banned: tired, exhausted, drained, low, foggy, heavy, rough, terrible. Each one gets replaced by a measurement: hours, percent, the count of times, minutes lost, number of attempts.
prompts.check: None of the eight banned words appear, and the piece contains at least nine numbers, each attached to a unit.

prompts.title: The Call That Ran Long
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about a discovery call booked for thirty minutes that ran to ninety-six. Cover what the founder said, what you did not say, and what the call turned out to be worth.
prompts.constraint: No adjective of degree anywhere. Every judgement of size, length, difficulty, or cost has to be a number. Minimum twenty-five numbers, at least twelve of them uneven.
prompts.check: Twenty-five or more numbers, twelve or more that do not end in zero or five, and no words from the intensifier family in the file.

prompts.title: Odd Numbers Only
prompts.prompt: Describe the state of your Figma file at 2:40am in under 150 words. Count the layers, the pages, the unnamed frames, the plugins running, the versions saved.
prompts.constraint: Every quantity is an exact figure you could verify by opening the file. Banned: about, around, roughly, nearly, or so, a few, several, many, countless.
prompts.check: Zero approximation words, and every noun of quantity in the piece carries an exact figure.

prompts.title: Guarantee With A Number
prompts.prompt: Write a 250 word guarantee section for your landing page service. Say what you promise, in what time, and exactly what happens if you miss it.
prompts.constraint: Six numbers minimum, including one day count, one rupee figure, one percentage, and one count of revisions. Banned: fast, quick, rapid, unlimited, hassle-free, seamless, industry-leading.
prompts.check: Six or more numbers covering all four required kinds, and none of the seven banned words appear.

prompts.title: A Week Counted
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about one real week of your life told only in quantities. Hours, rupees, messages, kilometres, cups of chai, calls, minutes of practice.
prompts.constraint: Every paragraph opens with a number. No paragraph may contain a degree adjective. At least forty numbers across the piece, at least twenty of them uneven.
prompts.check: Every paragraph begins with a digit or a written number, forty or more numbers total, twenty or more not round, and zero degree adjectives.

prompts.title: Counting The Mala
prompts.prompt: Write 650 words about your japa across the last thirty days. You may not describe the practice as good, deep, dry, or difficult.
prompts.constraint: Only counts and clock times may carry the judgement: rounds, minutes, days missed, the hour you sat, the number of times the mind left. Every quality word applied to the practice is banned.
prompts.check: Zero quality adjectives attached to the practice, and at least eighteen counts or clock times, eight or more of them uneven.

prompts.title: Seventeen, Not Many
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words about the clients you have said no to this year and why. Every reason has to arrive as a number.
prompts.constraint: Exactly seventeen numbers inside 150 words. No number may repeat. At least ten must be uneven.
prompts.check: Seventeen distinct numbers, zero repeats, ten or more not round, and the piece stays under 150 words.

prompts.title: The Arithmetic Of The Agency
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words on the real economics of your agency for someone who wants to start one. What came in, what went out, and what your hour is actually worth.
prompts.constraint: No adjective of size, quality, or difficulty anywhere. Every claim rides on a figure. Include at least eight figures that are uncomfortable to publish, and round nothing for comfort.
prompts.check: Zero size, quality, or difficulty adjectives, sixty or more numbers, and no figure ending in three or more zeroes unless it is a real invoice amount.

prompts.title: Proof Page With Figures
prompts.prompt: Write a 1,000 word results page for your agency built on three case studies. Use real structure and leave the client names out if you need to.
prompts.constraint: Every sentence containing a claim must contain a number. Banned: significant, dramatic, massive, huge, impressive, remarkable, game-changing, transformative. Each case study needs a before number, an after number, and a duration.
prompts.check: Every claim sentence carries a figure, all three case studies show before, after, and duration, and zero banned words appear.

prompts.title: Everything I Did Not Do
prompts.prompt: Write 1,000 words about the gap between what you planned for this year and what actually happened. Count out every gap in full.
prompts.constraint: At least twenty planned-versus-actual pairs, woven into prose rather than laid out in a table. No word may soften a gap: no just, only, merely, barely, at least.
prompts.check: Twenty or more planned-actual pairs, all inside prose, and zero softener words in the file.

prompts.title: The Biggest Day, Flatly
prompts.prompt: Write 140 words about the day your first international client paid. Say it in the register you would use for buying milk.
prompts.constraint: No exclamation marks. No word warmer than the word fine. Banned: amazing, unbelievable, insane, crazy, life-changing, dream, finally, wild. The last line must be a clock time or a measurement.
prompts.check: Zero banned words, zero exclamation marks, and the final line contains only a time, a date, or a measured quantity.

prompts.title: Quiet Claim, Big Number
prompts.prompt: Write a 150 word results block for a page where the outcome is genuinely large. A client went from eleven leads a month to a hundred and forty-eight. Say it without raising your voice.
prompts.constraint: The bigger the number, the flatter the sentence around it. No adjective may sit within three words of any figure. The section ends on a measurement rather than a statement of value.
prompts.check: No adjective within three words of any figure, and the last sentence is a measurement.

prompts.title: A Small Word For It
prompts.prompt: Write 130 words about the first time something happened in practice that you have never been able to describe. Use the plainest words you own and stop before you start explaining.
prompts.constraint: No word longer than two syllables. No metaphor and no comparison of any kind. The entry closes on the clock time you got up.
prompts.check: Every word is one or two syllables, there is no comparison anywhere, and the final line is a clock time.

prompts.title: Fever, Three Days
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about being ill alone in your room for three days while a client launch was live. Keep the temperature of the language below the temperature of the events.
prompts.constraint: No sentence may contain more than one adjective. Every peak in the story closes on a number: a temperature, a clock time, a dosage, a step count. Every word for suffering is banned.
prompts.check: One adjective maximum per sentence, and each of the three days ends on a measured figure.

prompts.title: Two Lakh In The Account
prompts.prompt: You cleared more than two lakh in one month for the first time. Write 150 words about the ninety minutes after you saw the number, in the tone of a delivery receipt.
prompts.constraint: Under 150 words. No adjective anywhere. Every emotional peak resolves into an action with a time attached. The last sentence is a clock time and nothing else.
prompts.check: Zero adjectives, at least four clock times, and a final sentence that is a time and nothing more.

prompts.title: Understated High Ticket Offer
prompts.prompt: Write a 300 word offer section for a three lakh landing page package. Write it so a serious buyer takes it more seriously because of how quiet it is.
prompts.constraint: No superlatives. No adjective before any noun that names a deliverable. Every benefit becomes a count or a date. The section closes on a delivery window in days.
prompts.check: Zero superlatives, no adjective before any deliverable noun, and the closing line is a day count.

prompts.title: The Day The Site Went Down
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about the launch day when the site was down for forty-one minutes in the middle of a paid campaign. Tell it in a register two sizes smaller than the event.
prompts.constraint: Banned: crisis, panic, disaster, nightmare, chaos, emergency. Every rise in stakes gets a shorter sentence and a smaller word. The essay ends on a measurement.
prompts.check: None of the six banned words appear, the longest sentence in the final third is under fifteen words, and the last line is a measurement.

prompts.title: The Week After Diksha
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about receiving diksha and what changed in the week after. Keep the language small enough that a careless reader could miss what happened.
prompts.constraint: No word from the vocabulary of transcendence: divine, sacred, profound, blessed, grace, transformation, awakening. The piece closes on a clock time paired with a physical detail.
prompts.check: Zero words from the banned list, no sentence longer than twenty words, and a closing line that pairs a time with an object.

prompts.title: Understate A Real Loss
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words about the biggest professional loss of the last two years. Use the tone of a courier tracking update.
prompts.constraint: Twelve sentences maximum. No adjective in any sentence that carries the loss. Every sentence containing a fact must contain a number or a date. The final sentence is a measurement.
prompts.check: Twelve or fewer sentences, no adjective in the loss sentences, and a measurement as the last sentence.

prompts.title: The Year Everything Moved
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words about the twelve months that changed your working life. Use the register of a maintenance log kept by somebody who does not care.
prompts.constraint: If you use section headers they must be dates. No sentence may carry two emotional words. Each of the six biggest moments resolves on a measurement rather than a reflection.
prompts.check: Six identified peaks, each closing on a measurement, and no sentence in the file carrying more than one emotional word.

prompts.title: Big Result, Small Voice
prompts.prompt: Write a 1,000 word case study page for a client whose monthly revenue went from four lakh to thirty-one lakh after a rebuild. The bigger the figure, the quieter the sentence around it.
prompts.constraint: The largest numbers get the plainest sentences. No adjective may appear in any sentence containing a figure above one lakh. No exclamation marks. The page closes on a date.
prompts.check: Every sentence with a figure above one lakh has zero adjectives, and the final line of the page is a date.

prompts.title: Say It Once, Small
prompts.prompt: Write 1,000 words about your relationship with your Guru. Not one sentence may try to convey how much it matters.
prompts.constraint: No superlative, no intensifier, no word of devotion. Everything is carried by facts, dates, distances, and things done. Close on a measurement.
prompts.check: Zero superlatives, intensifiers, or devotional words, at least fifteen dated or measured facts, and a measured final line.

prompts.title: Shortest At The Worst
prompts.prompt: Write 140 words about the moment your father asked what you actually do for money. Let the language get simpler word by word as you reach his question.
prompts.constraint: The final three sentences may use one-syllable words only. Everything before them may use anything. No sentence after the peak may run past seven words.
prompts.check: The last three sentences contain only one-syllable words and none of them exceeds seven words.

prompts.title: Plain At The Ask
prompts.prompt: Write four versions of a call to action block for a high-ticket landing page service. Each version warms up in ordinary marketing language and drops into plain speech at the ask.
prompts.constraint: Every version's final two sentences use only one and two-syllable words and contain no word from marketing vocabulary.
prompts.check: Four versions, each ending on two sentences with no word above two syllables and no marketing term.

prompts.title: The Line I Avoided
prompts.prompt: Write 130 words about a moment in practice you have been avoiding writing about. Let the language shrink as you get closer to it.
prompts.constraint: Sentence length must fall from the first sentence to the last with no exceptions. The final sentence is five words or fewer and entirely one-syllable.
prompts.check: Each sentence is shorter in words than the one before it, and the last is five words or fewer with only monosyllables.

prompts.title: The Night Someone Was Ill
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about a night when someone at home was ill and you were the one awake. Keep the vocabulary ordinary and let it get more ordinary as the night gets worse.
prompts.constraint: Split the piece into 100 word blocks. From the halfway point onward, every block must have a lower average syllables-per-word than the block before it. The last block averages under 1.3.
prompts.check: Compute the average syllable count of each block. Every block after halfway is lower than the one before, and the last is under 1.3.

prompts.title: One Syllable Ending
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words about the moment you knew a friendship was over. Use any language you like for the first 120 words.
prompts.constraint: The last 30 words contain only one-syllable words. No name may appear in those 30 words. No question anywhere in them.
prompts.check: The final 30 words are all monosyllables, contain no proper noun, and contain no question mark.

prompts.title: The Guarantee, Plainly
prompts.prompt: Write a 250 word risk reversal section for your service. The first half can be as polished as you like. The promise itself has to be completely plain.
prompts.constraint: The promise sentence uses only one-syllable words and stays under twelve words. Nothing may follow it except at most one more sentence.
prompts.check: The promise sentence is under twelve words and fully monosyllabic, and at most one sentence follows it.

prompts.title: The Call You Handled Badly
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about a client call you handled badly. Build it so the language is at its most complex in the setup and at its plainest at the point of your mistake.
prompts.constraint: Mark the peak sentence. Everything within fifty words on either side of it uses one and two-syllable words only. The setup must contain at least six words of three or more syllables, all before the halfway mark.
prompts.check: Six or more long words, all in the first half, and a 100 word window around the marked peak containing nothing above two syllables.

prompts.title: When The Mind Went Quiet
prompts.prompt: Write 650 words about the quietest minute you have had in practice. Approach it in ordinary language and arrive at it with the plainest words you own.
prompts.constraint: The paragraph describing that minute contains no word above one syllable, runs to no more than forty words, and contains no Sanskrit.
prompts.check: The peak paragraph is forty words or fewer, entirely monosyllabic, and contains no Sanskrit term.

prompts.title: Descend To Plain
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words about being told no by someone whose yes you wanted. Start in your normal writing voice and end in the voice you use when you are actually upset.
prompts.constraint: Three paragraphs. Average word length must fall in each one. The final paragraph runs under twenty-five words and uses only one-syllable words.
prompts.check: Three paragraphs with falling average word length, and a last paragraph under twenty-five words with only monosyllables.

prompts.title: The Hardest Thing, Plainly Said
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words about the hardest thing that has happened to you since you turned eighteen. Give yourself the full range in the setup and take all of it away at the centre.
prompts.constraint: Identify the emotional peak. From there to the end, no word above two syllables and no sentence above twelve words. Before it, at least fifteen words of three or more syllables.
prompts.check: Fifteen long words before the marked peak, zero after it, and no sentence after it running past twelve words.

prompts.title: Long Page, Plain Peak
prompts.prompt: Write a 1,000 word sales page for something you believe in and price high. The page can be as crafted as you like except at the two points where you ask for money.
prompts.constraint: Both ask sections contain only one-syllable words and run under forty words each. Neither may contain a marketing verb: unlock, discover, transform, elevate, accelerate.
prompts.check: Two ask blocks, each under forty words, entirely monosyllabic, and containing none of the five banned verbs.

prompts.title: Plain Words For A Guru
prompts.prompt: Write 1,000 words about why you took a Guru, for a reader who thinks it is a weakness. Let the argument be as sophisticated as you can make it and the moment of admission be plain.
prompts.constraint: The admission is one paragraph under thirty words, entirely one-syllable, with no Sanskrit, no honorific, and no abstraction. Everything before it may argue at full complexity.
prompts.check: One paragraph under thirty words with only monosyllables, no Sanskrit and no honorific, positioned after at least 700 words of argument.

prompts.title: We Break, You Fix
prompts.prompt: Write 140 words on why designers keep redesigning instead of shipping. Diagnose the fault as something all of us do, then turn and tell one person what to do about it.
prompts.constraint: The first half uses only we, us, our. The second half uses only you and your. Exactly one sentence marks the crossover. The word I may not appear.
prompts.check: No first person singular in the file, a clean split with exactly one crossover sentence, and no we after the crossover.

prompts.title: One Clean Crossover
prompts.prompt: Write a 150 word problem and solution block for founders who keep rebuilding their site instead of fixing the offer. They have paid for three redesigns in two years.
prompts.constraint: Diagnose in we, prescribe in you, and name the people who get it right in the third person. Exactly one crossover sentence. Zero uses of I.
prompts.check: Three pronoun zones in that order, one crossover sentence, and no I anywhere in the file.

prompts.title: Our Fault, Your Move
prompts.prompt: Write 130 words about how easily attention slips during japa. Own it as a shared human problem first, then instruct yourself in the second person.
prompts.constraint: The first seventy words use we-form pronouns only. Everything after uses you-form only. One crossover sentence. Ban I, me, and my entirely.
prompts.check: Words 1 to 70 carry only we-form pronouns, the rest only you-form, and no singular first person appears.

prompts.title: Why We Ship Late
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words on why young designers ship late. Aim it at one reader who is doing it at this exact moment.
prompts.constraint: The diagnosis uses we at least eight times. The prescription uses you at least eight times. A third section ranks three practitioners in the third person. Exactly one crossover sentence in the whole piece.
prompts.check: Eight or more uses of we, eight or more of you, three third-person examples, and exactly one sentence containing both we and you.

prompts.title: The Ranking Paragraph
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words that diagnose a habit you share with every freelancer. Prescribe the fix to one person. Then rank three people you have watched handle it well.
prompts.constraint: Three sentences of diagnosis in we, three of prescription in you, three of ranking in the third person. Nine sentences total and no more.
prompts.check: Exactly nine sentences in three groups of three, each group using only its assigned pronoun.

prompts.title: Diagnose Us, Instruct You
prompts.prompt: Write 500 words about a week where nothing shipped and you know exactly why. Diagnose it as a thing all of us do, then turn and instruct one person.
prompts.constraint: The first 300 words use we-form pronouns only. Everything after uses you-form only. One crossover sentence. No I, me, or my anywhere.
prompts.check: Zero singular first person, exactly one crossover sentence, and no we-form pronoun after it.

prompts.title: What We Get Wrong About Money
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about how people in their twenties think about money. Use your own numbers as the evidence and never as the subject.
prompts.constraint: The whole diagnosis is in we, even where the mistake is only yours. The advice is in you. Rank three approaches in the third person. One crossover sentence, placed after the halfway point.
prompts.check: One crossover sentence located after the 450 word mark, with we used exclusively before it in the diagnosis and you exclusively in the advice.

prompts.title: We The Distracted
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about the modern mind and mantra. Write from inside the problem instead of above it.
prompts.constraint: Never use I. Diagnose the difficulty in we for the first 400 words. Prescribe in you for the next 250. Close by ranking three approaches in the third person in about 50 words.
prompts.check: Zero uses of I, three zones at roughly the required lengths, and exactly one crossover sentence.

prompts.title: The Turn On The Page
prompts.prompt: Write a 400 word mid-page section for a service you sell. The whole section exists to earn one sentence: the one that turns from we to you.
prompts.constraint: The crossover sentence contains both pronouns, runs under fifteen words, and is the shortest sentence on the page. Write six candidate versions of it and mark the one you keep.
prompts.check: Six candidates listed, and the kept one is under fifteen words, carries both pronouns, and is shorter than every other sentence in the section.

prompts.title: The Craft We Are Ruining
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words about what AI is doing to design work. No reader may feel attacked and one reader has to feel instructed.
prompts.constraint: Four movements: shared fault in we, one crossover, instruction in you, then a ranked third-person section naming who is handling it well and who is not. Zero uses of I in the first 800 words.
prompts.check: One crossover sentence, no I before word 800, and a ranking section in third person naming at least three parties.

prompts.title: Full Page, Three Pronouns
prompts.prompt: Write a 1,000 word landing page for a productised service. The audience is defensive about the setup they already paid for.
prompts.constraint: Every problem statement in we. Every instruction and call to action in you. Every proof in the third person. Exactly one crossover sentence on the whole page.
prompts.check: Scan each section for pronouns: problems contain zero you, calls to action contain zero we, proofs contain neither, and one crossover exists.

prompts.title: Twelve Crossovers, One Kept
prompts.prompt: Write twelve versions of the same 140 word piece about doubt at twenty-one. Each version puts the crossover from we to you in a different place.
prompts.constraint: Twelve versions, each under 150 words, each with exactly one crossover sentence. No version may use I. Rank all twelve at the bottom with a one-line reason for the winner.
prompts.check: Twelve versions with twelve different crossover positions, zero uses of I, and a ranked list carrying a one-line reason.

prompts.title: Paid, Claimed, Bounded
prompts.prompt: Write four blocks of three sentences each. Every block covers something you learned the hard way in client work.
prompts.constraint: Sentence one names the cost with a number and zero adjectives. Sentence two makes the claim. Sentence three bounds it, naming who or when it does not apply. Twelve sentences in total.
prompts.check: Twelve sentences in four groups of three, each first sentence carrying a figure and no adjective, each third sentence containing a limiting word such as unless, except, only when, or for.

prompts.title: Earned Claim Block
prompts.prompt: Write a 150 word credibility block for your agency page. Build it on the cost, claim, limit structure and nothing else.
prompts.constraint: One number for what it cost you in months or rupees, one claim, one boundary. No adjective in the cost sentence. The boundary must shrink your market rather than widen it.
prompts.check: The cost sentence carries a figure and no adjective, and the boundary sentence names a group you will not serve.

prompts.title: What It Took
prompts.prompt: Write 130 words about something your practice has actually taught you. Price it honestly before you claim it.
prompts.constraint: Open with the count of days, rounds, hours, or months, and no adjective in that sentence. Then the claim. Then the limit, which must be about your own experience rather than a general caveat.
prompts.check: The first sentence carries a count and zero adjectives, and the last sentence limits the claim to your specific case.

prompts.title: Three Years, One Claim
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words making one argument about landing pages. It has to be an argument you have paid for in real work.
prompts.constraint: Exactly five cost-claim-limit units, spread evenly. Every cost sentence carries a number and no adjective. Every limit names a condition under which you would be wrong.
prompts.check: Five units, five numbered costs, zero adjectives in the cost sentences, and five limits you could actually be caught out by.

prompts.title: One Number, One Limit
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words about pricing. Build the whole thing on one thing you got wrong and paid for.
prompts.constraint: Exactly one number in the whole piece and it must be the cost. Exactly one claim sentence. Exactly one limit sentence. Everything else is context.
prompts.check: One number in the file, and the last two sentences are the claim and the limit in that order.

prompts.title: Priced, Claimed, Fenced
prompts.prompt: Write 500 words about one thing this year taught you about your own work. Price it, claim it, then fence it.
prompts.constraint: Three cost-claim-limit units. Every cost sentence opens with a number and carries no adjective. Every limit names a person or a week where the claim would have failed.
prompts.check: Three units, three adjective-free numbered costs, and three limits each naming a specific person or week.

prompts.title: The Fee I Refunded
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about a refund you issued. Cover what it taught you and the point where that lesson stops being true.
prompts.constraint: Eight cost-claim-limit units. The costs must use at least three different units of measure: rupees, days, and one more you can count. No adjective may appear in any cost sentence.
prompts.check: Eight units, three distinct measures used across them, and zero adjectives in all eight cost sentences.

prompts.title: What Sadhana Cost
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words on what the practice has cost you in hours, sleep, and social life. Say what you claim from that, then say where the claim stops.
prompts.constraint: Three costs with exact counts and no adjectives. One claim. Two limits, one of which must concede that someone with far less practice may understand more than you.
prompts.check: Three numbered cost sentences without adjectives, one clear claim, and two limits including the required concession.

prompts.title: Six Limits On A Page
prompts.prompt: Write a 400 word section for your service page made of six cost, claim, limit units. Every limit has to shrink your market rather than widen it.
prompts.constraint: Six units. Each limit is six words or fewer. Each cost carries a number and no adjective. The six limits together must disqualify at least three types of buyer.
prompts.check: Six units, six limits of six words or fewer, six numbered adjective-free costs, and three buyer types disqualified.

prompts.title: Everything I Am Sure Of
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words listing the things you actually believe about work. Every belief gets priced and bounded.
prompts.constraint: Twelve units. No two consecutive costs may use the same unit of measure. Every limit must name a real person, a kind of person, or a situation where the claim fails.
prompts.check: Twelve units, no repeated measure back to back, and twelve limits each naming a specific exception.

prompts.title: The Honest Sales Page
prompts.prompt: Write a 1,000 word sales page that disqualifies more readers than it invites. Every claim on it has to be paid for and fenced.
prompts.constraint: Every section carries a cost, a claim, and a limit. At least six limits across the page. The page must name at least three types of buyer you refuse to work with.
prompts.check: Six or more limits, three named refusals, and every claim preceded by a numbered cost with no adjectives.

prompts.title: One Belief, Fifteen Drafts
prompts.prompt: Take one thing being twenty-one makes you sure of. Write it fifteen times as a 120 word cost, claim, limit unit, changing only the cost you name.
prompts.constraint: Fifteen drafts, each under 150 words. Fifteen different costs, all carrying numbers and no adjectives. The claim stays word for word identical across all fifteen.
prompts.check: Fifteen drafts with an identical claim sentence, fifteen distinct numbered costs, and zero adjectives in any cost sentence.

prompts.title: Kitchen Vehicles Only
prompts.prompt: Write 140 words about how a landing page should be structured. Use three analogies drawn only from your mother's kitchen.
prompts.constraint: Each analogy runs two sentences and stops. No analogy may be mentioned again. Vehicles must come from cooking, vessels, or ingredients. Nothing from sport, war, or software.
prompts.check: Three analogies, each exactly two sentences, none referred to again after it ends, all drawn from the kitchen.

prompts.title: Humble Vehicle, Short Cut
prompts.prompt: Write three versions of a sixty word section explaining what a landing page audit finds. Each uses one analogy from a domain simpler than websites.
prompts.constraint: Allowed vehicles: cooking, a bicycle, a ceiling fan, a street dog, a toddler, rain. Two sentences each, no callback, no extended metaphor.
prompts.check: Three versions, each with one two-sentence analogy from the allowed list, and no return to it afterwards.

prompts.title: The Mind Is A Goat
prompts.prompt: Write 130 words about the wandering mind during japa. Use one analogy taken from animals people actually keep or see on the street.
prompts.constraint: Two sentences of analogy and no more. The animal must be one you have seen in an Indian street or home. Never mention that animal again in the piece.
prompts.check: Exactly two sentences of analogy, one named animal, and zero further mentions of it.

prompts.title: Conversion And The Pressure Cooker
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words explaining how conversion rate actually works. Every analogy has to come from a household you have lived in.
prompts.constraint: Five analogies. Two sentences each. Each from a different humble domain: kitchen, weather, animals, children, hand tools. No analogy may be extended, revisited, or turned into a running theme.
prompts.check: Five analogies from five distinct domains, two sentences each, and zero callbacks anywhere in the essay.

prompts.title: Two Sentences, Then Gone
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words about why clients ask for the logo to be bigger. Use one analogy that lands and then disappears completely.
prompts.constraint: One analogy of exactly two sentences, placed in the middle. The vehicle must be humbler than the subject. The rest of the text may not use any noun from the analogy.
prompts.check: One two-sentence analogy, and none of its nouns appear anywhere else in the piece.

prompts.title: Household Objects, Inner Weather
prompts.prompt: Write 500 words about the state of your head this week. Every abstraction has to be carried by an object from your own home.
prompts.constraint: Four analogies, two sentences each, from four different household objects. No analogy may be revisited and none may run past its second sentence.
prompts.check: Four two-sentence analogies from four distinct household objects, and zero callbacks.

prompts.title: Teaching Through Weather
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about how a business gets its first ten clients. Weather is your only source of analogy.
prompts.constraint: Seven analogies, all from weather, each exactly two sentences. No two may use the same weather condition. Never call one back.
prompts.check: Seven weather analogies, seven distinct conditions, two sentences each, and zero callbacks.

prompts.title: Children And Concentration
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about training concentration. Small children are your only analogy source, including your brother when he was small.
prompts.constraint: Six analogies, two sentences each, all about behaviour you have actually watched. No analogy may become a running theme and none may be revisited.
prompts.check: Six analogies of two sentences each, all about observed child behaviour, and zero callbacks.

prompts.title: Machine Analogies For Buyers
prompts.prompt: Write a 400 word section for a service page explaining why a broken funnel is a plumbing problem rather than a design problem. Use only machines you have personally operated.
prompts.constraint: Three analogies of two sentences each, all from machines you have touched. No abstract machine language such as engines, systems, or pipelines. No callbacks.
prompts.check: Three named machines you have operated, two sentences each, zero abstract machine words, and no returns.

prompts.title: An Argument In Humble Pictures
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words arguing that most founders should not redesign their site. Carry the whole argument on twelve analogies.
prompts.constraint: Twelve analogies, two sentences each, from four domains only: kitchen, animals, children, weather. Three per domain. No callbacks, no extended metaphors, and no analogy in the first or last 100 words.
prompts.check: Twelve analogies, three per domain across four domains, all two sentences, and none in the opening or closing 100 words.

prompts.title: Sales Page, Humble Pictures
prompts.prompt: Write a 1,000 word sales page for a high-ticket service. Every section carries one analogy drawn from work your buyer thinks is beneath them.
prompts.constraint: Six analogies of two sentences each, from six lower-paid trades: cooking, driving, repair, tailoring, farming, cleaning. No callbacks.
prompts.check: Six two-sentence analogies from six distinct trades, no callbacks, and no sentence in the file that treats a trade as simple or unskilled.

prompts.title: Eight Trades, One Lesson
prompts.prompt: Write eight versions of the same 140 word entry about being taught by somebody far ahead of you. Each version uses a different trade as its only analogy.
prompts.constraint: Eight versions, each under 150 words, drawn from tailoring, carpentry, cooking, driving, masonry, barbering, welding, and farming. Two sentences of analogy per version, no callbacks, no spiritual metaphor.
prompts.check: Eight versions from eight trades, each with one two-sentence analogy, zero spiritual metaphors, and zero callbacks.

prompts.title: Claim, Picture, Claim Again
prompts.prompt: Write five units about client work. Each one makes a claim, then shows a picture, then makes the same claim again using the picture's own noun.
prompts.constraint: Three sentences per unit. The third sentence must contain a noun that first appeared in the second. The third may not reuse any noun from the first.
prompts.check: Five units, each third sentence carrying a noun from its own second sentence and none from its first.

prompts.title: Restate With The Object
prompts.prompt: Write four hero blocks for four different services. Each states the promise, shows a physical scene, then restates the promise in the language of that scene.
prompts.constraint: Three lines per block. The restatement must borrow at least one noun and one verb from the scene line. No two blocks may use the same scene.
prompts.check: Four blocks, each restatement borrowing a noun and a verb from its own image line.

prompts.title: The Image Says It Better
prompts.prompt: Write 130 words on one thing you have understood about attention. Use this shape exactly once: claim, image, restated claim.
prompts.constraint: The image must come from today, not from a book. The restatement must be shorter than the original claim and must contain the image's central noun.
prompts.check: The restatement is shorter than the claim and contains the main noun of the image.

prompts.title: Six Turns In Seven Hundred
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words on why most landing pages fail. Build it as six re-claim units and nothing else.
prompts.constraint: Six units. Each claim is under twenty words, each image runs one to three sentences, each restatement is under twelve words and carries the image's noun. No other material in the essay.
prompts.check: Six units in the required shape, with all six restatements under twelve words and containing their image noun.

prompts.title: Picture, Then Prove It
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words about why you work at night. One claim, one long image, one restatement.
prompts.constraint: The image must run at least eighty words and contain no argument at all. The restatement must be under ten words and use two nouns from the image.
prompts.check: The image is eighty words or more with zero claims in it, and the closing line is under ten words with two image nouns.

prompts.title: Claim It With The Object
prompts.prompt: Write 450 words about one thing you have understood about your own attention this month. Every claim gets an image and then gets remade in that image's own noun.
prompts.constraint: Four units. Every image comes from this week and none from a book. Every restatement is shorter than its claim and carries the image's central noun.
prompts.check: Four units, four restatements shorter than their claims, each containing its own image's main noun.

prompts.title: The Argument In Pictures
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words making one argument about ambition. Every claim is followed by an image and then remade in that image's own terms.
prompts.constraint: Eight units. No image may be repeated or referred to later. Every restatement must be shorter than its claim and must contain no abstract noun.
prompts.check: Eight units, eight restatements shorter than their claims, and zero abstract nouns across all restatements.

prompts.title: What The Mala Teaches
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about repetition. Use objects from your own practice as the images and never explain them.
prompts.constraint: Six units. The images must be physical: beads, the mat, the clock, the window, the glass of water, the light. Each restatement must use the object as the subject of the sentence.
prompts.check: Six restatements, each with a physical object as its grammatical subject.

prompts.title: One Noun Sells It
prompts.prompt: Write a 400 word section for a page selling a service you offer. One claim, one scene, one restatement, and a single noun carries the whole thing.
prompts.constraint: The chosen noun appears exactly twice: once in the scene and once in the restatement. It may never appear in the claim. Write four versions with four different nouns.
prompts.check: Four versions, each with its key noun appearing exactly twice in the two required positions and never in the claim.

prompts.title: Twelve Claims, Twelve Objects
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words about what you have learned running an agency at twenty-one. Build it as twelve re-claim units.
prompts.constraint: Twelve units with twelve different physical images. No image may come from a screen, an app, or a piece of software. Every restatement uses the image's noun and contains no adjective.
prompts.check: Twelve units, twelve non-digital images, and twelve adjective-free restatements each containing its image noun.

prompts.title: Whole Page, Restated
prompts.prompt: Write a 1,000 word landing page for a service you actually sell. Every section makes its claim, shows a scene, then remakes the claim in the scene's words.
prompts.constraint: Seven sections. Every restatement doubles as that section's subhead and must work when read on its own. No section may reuse another section's noun.
prompts.check: Seven restatements pulled out as subheads read as a coherent list of promises with no repeated nouns.

prompts.title: Ten Images For Belief
prompts.prompt: Write ten versions of the same 130 word entry about belief. Each version keeps the same claim and swaps in a different image from your own week.
prompts.constraint: Ten versions, each under 150 words. No image from scripture and none from a book. Every restatement is under eight words and uses the image's noun.
prompts.check: Ten versions with an identical claim, ten different lived images, and ten restatements under eight words each carrying its image noun.

prompts.title: Say It, Then Weigh It
prompts.prompt: Write three short anecdotes of about forty-five words each from client work. Each ends on something somebody actually said out loud.
prompts.constraint: Repeat the spoken line word for word, add a colon, then a principle of twelve words or fewer. Nothing may change in the repeat, including punctuation inside the line.
prompts.check: Three repeats identical character for character to the original lines, and three principles of twelve words or fewer.

prompts.title: Objection, Echoed Back
prompts.prompt: Write three blocks of about fifty words for a sales page. Each one is built on a real thing a prospect has said to you.
prompts.constraint: Each block ends on the quoted objection, then repeats it word for word, then a colon, then a principle of twelve words maximum that reframes it.
prompts.check: Three word-for-word repeats and three principles under thirteen words, each reframing the objection instead of answering it.

prompts.title: What He Actually Said
prompts.prompt: Write 130 words about something your father, mother, or brother said to you. It has to be a line you have not stopped thinking about.
prompts.constraint: The anecdote ends on the line of speech. Then the line again, exactly. Then a colon and a principle of twelve words maximum. Nothing after that.
prompts.check: The file ends with the repeated line, a colon, and twelve words or fewer.

prompts.title: Five Voices, Five Pivots
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words made of five anecdotes about learning to work. Each one ends on speech.
prompts.constraint: Five echo-pivots. Each spoken line comes from a different person. No principle may exceed twelve words. No principle may begin with the word This.
prompts.check: Five word-for-word repeats from five different speakers, five principles of twelve words or fewer, none starting with This.

prompts.title: One Line, Said Twice
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words about the shortest useful thing a client ever said to you. It should be a line you still repeat to other people.
prompts.constraint: The quoted line is six words or fewer. It appears exactly twice: at the end of the anecdote and at the start of the pivot. The principle is eight words or fewer.
prompts.check: One line of six words or fewer appearing exactly twice, followed by a principle of eight words or fewer.

prompts.title: The Line I Kept
prompts.prompt: Write 450 words about three things said to you this month that you have not been able to drop. Each anecdote ends on the line itself.
prompts.constraint: Three echo-pivots. Each spoken line is repeated word for word, then a colon, then a principle of twelve words or fewer. No principle may explain the line.
prompts.check: Three word-for-word repeats and three principles of twelve words or fewer that add something rather than explain.

prompts.title: Things People Told Me
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about advice you were given at nineteen and twenty. Half of it turned out to be wrong.
prompts.constraint: Seven anecdotes and seven echo-pivots. At least three principles must contradict the line they repeat. No principle over twelve words and no anecdote over 100 words.
prompts.check: Seven word-for-word repeats, three of them followed by a contradicting principle, and all principles under thirteen words.

prompts.title: The Guru's One Sentence
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about one sentence you read or heard from your Guru. It has to be one that changed something concrete in your week.
prompts.constraint: The quoted line stays exactly as it appears in the source. It appears at the end of the anecdote and again at the pivot. The principle is your own, twelve words or fewer, and contains no Sanskrit.
prompts.check: The quote matches the source word for word in both positions, and the principle is in your own words, twelve or fewer, with no Sanskrit.

prompts.title: Objections Echoed On Page
prompts.prompt: Write a 400 word section for a sales page built from four real things prospects have said to you. Each block ends on the objection and pivots off it.
prompts.constraint: Four echo-pivots. Each spoken line runs under eight words and is repeated word for word. Each principle runs under nine words. No invented quotes.
prompts.check: Four word-for-word repeats of lines under eight words, four principles under nine words, and every quote traceable to a real conversation.

prompts.title: A Year In Ten Sentences
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words covering a year. Use ten things other people said to you as the entire structure.
prompts.constraint: Ten anecdotes and ten echo-pivots. Every principle is twelve words or fewer. No two principles may share a main verb. The last principle is six words or fewer.
prompts.check: Ten word-for-word repeats, ten principles under thirteen words with ten distinct main verbs, and a final principle of six words or fewer.

prompts.title: Page Built On Speech
prompts.prompt: Write a 1,000 word landing page for a service you sell. Every section is an anecdote ending on something a customer said.
prompts.constraint: Six sections and six echo-pivots. Every principle also appears as a heading elsewhere on the page and must be twelve words or fewer. No invented quotes.
prompts.check: Six word-for-word repeats, six principles reused as headings, all twelve words or fewer, and every quote traceable to a real conversation.

prompts.title: Brother, Eight Ways
prompts.prompt: Take eight things your younger brother has actually said to you. Write each one as a separate 130 word piece that ends on his line and pivots off it.
prompts.constraint: Eight pieces, each under 150 words. His grammar stays exactly as he said it. Every principle is twelve words or fewer and may never explain the joke or the pain.
prompts.check: Eight pieces with word-for-word repeats and his original grammar intact, and eight principles of twelve words or fewer.

prompts.title: Ten Cold Openings
prompts.prompt: Write ten opening sentences for ten different pieces from your own life. One about the agency, one about your brother, one about money, one about illness, one about practice, and five you pick.
prompts.constraint: Every opening begins with a person, a hard fact, a date, or a clock time. No weather, no room description, no throat-clearing. The first word may not be an article or a preposition.
prompts.check: Ten openings, each starting with a name, a number, a date, or a person, and none starting with the, a, it, or there.

prompts.title: First Line, No Warm-Up
prompts.prompt: Write eight opening lines for eight landing pages. Use categories you have actually worked in.
prompts.constraint: Each first line names a person, a price, a date, or a measurable fact. Ban every opener beginning with In today's, We believe, Imagine, What if, or Are you.
prompts.check: Eight lines, zero banned openers, and each containing a proper noun or a number inside the first six words.

prompts.title: The Clock Comes First
prompts.prompt: Write six journal openings from six different mornings of the past month. Each one starts before you are properly awake.
prompts.constraint: Every one opens with a clock time, and the next thing is a person or an action, never a state of mind. Each is under twenty words.
prompts.check: Six openings, each starting with a time, each under twenty words, and none containing a feeling word.

prompts.title: Cold Open, Seven Hundred Words
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about your first paid client. The first sentence has to be doing work before the reader knows what the piece is about.
prompts.constraint: The first sentence names a person and contains a number. Nothing in the first 100 words may explain what the essay is about. No scene setting, no weather, no time of year.
prompts.check: The first sentence carries a name and a figure, and the first 100 words contain no statement of topic.

prompts.title: No Runway At All
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words about a day you failed at something. Start at the moment of the failure and give the reader no runway.
prompts.constraint: The first sentence is the hardest fact in the piece. No background before it and none for the following fifty words. No sentence anywhere may begin with It was.
prompts.check: The opening sentence contains the central fact, and no It was construction appears in the file.

prompts.title: Six Mornings, Cold
prompts.prompt: Write six journal entries of about eighty words each from six mornings this month. Every one starts on a hard fact and never warms up.
prompts.constraint: Each entry opens with a person, a hard fact, a date, or a clock time. No entry may contain a feeling word in its first thirty words. No weather anywhere in the file.
prompts.check: Six entries in the four permitted opening forms, no feeling word in any first thirty words, and no weather in the file.

prompts.title: Date, Person, Hard Fact
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about the year you started your agency. Open on a date and a person inside the same sentence.
prompts.constraint: The first sentence carries a date and a name and no adjectives. The first paragraph contains no abstractions. The word journey is banned from the whole essay.
prompts.check: An opening sentence with both a date and a name and zero adjectives, and a first paragraph with no abstract nouns.

prompts.title: Cold Open On Practice
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about a sitting that did not go well. Open on the clock and stay factual for as long as you can.
prompts.constraint: The first word is a time. The first 150 words contain no interpretation at all, only what happened and when. No Sanskrit before word 150.
prompts.check: The first word is a time, the first 150 words are purely factual, and no Sanskrit appears inside them.

prompts.title: Twelve Cold Page Openers
prompts.prompt: Write twelve opening blocks of about thirty words each for twelve landing pages. Each one opens cold and earns its second sentence.
prompts.constraint: Three open on a person, three on a hard fact, three on a date, three on a clock time. Ban every opener starting with In today's, We believe, Imagine, What if, or Are you.
prompts.check: Twelve blocks in four groups of three, zero banned openers, and a proper noun or a number inside the first six words of each.

prompts.title: The Whole Thing, No Preamble
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words about the hardest client relationship you have had. The first sentence must carry more information than any other sentence in the piece.
prompts.constraint: Open on a person and a number with nothing before them. No paragraph may begin with a transition word. Ban But, However, So, And, and Now at the start of any paragraph.
prompts.check: The opening line carries a person and a figure, and no paragraph begins with any of the five banned transitions.

prompts.title: Long Page, Cold Sections
prompts.prompt: Write a 1,000 word landing page for a service you sell. Every single section has to open cold.
prompts.constraint: Eight sections. Every section's first sentence names a person, states a hard fact, gives a date, or gives a clock time. No section may open with a question or restate its own heading.
prompts.check: Eight section openings, all in the four permitted forms, and none of them a question.

prompts.title: Fifteen Openings, One Life
prompts.prompt: Write fifteen versions of the same 130 word piece about your life so far. Each version opens on a different hard fact.
prompts.constraint: Fifteen versions, each under 150 words. Each opening runs under twelve words and contains a number. The word life may not appear in any of them.
prompts.check: Fifteen versions with fifteen different numbered openings under twelve words, and zero uses of the word life.

prompts.title: Ten Endings That Refuse
prompts.prompt: Write ten final lines for ten pieces from your own life. Each one has to leave the reader holding something you never take back off them.
prompts.constraint: No line may summarise, resolve, moralise, or thank. Banned: so, therefore, in the end, ultimately, lesson. Each line under fifteen words.
prompts.check: Ten lines, all under fifteen words, none containing a banned word, and none stating a conclusion.

prompts.title: Open Ending, Real CTA
prompts.prompt: Write five closing blocks of about thirty words for five landing pages. Each ends on something unresolved and still asks for the click.
prompts.constraint: The last sentence before the button may not resolve anything. No urgency language, no scarcity, no summary of benefits.
prompts.check: Five closings, each ending on an open question, an unfinished fact, or a consequence you never name, with the call to action still present.

prompts.title: Stop Before The Lesson
prompts.prompt: Write 130 words about something that happened this week. Then delete the last two sentences and stop where the deletion leaves you.
prompts.constraint: The finished piece has no lesson, no realisation, and no naming of what you learned. It must end on an action or a fact.
prompts.check: The final sentence is an action or a fact, and the words realised, learned, understood, and taught appear nowhere.

prompts.title: The Unresolved Client
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about a working relationship that never got a proper ending. Neither of you ever said it was over.
prompts.constraint: The last paragraph runs three sentences or fewer and may not refer to anything earlier in the piece. It may not use the word still. Nothing may be summarised.
prompts.check: A final paragraph of three sentences or fewer that refers to nothing earlier and contains no summary or moral.

prompts.title: The Question Left Open
prompts.prompt: Write 450 words about money and your family. End on a question that the entry never answers.
prompts.constraint: The question is about one specific person, not about life in general. It runs under ten words. Nothing follows it and no paragraph anywhere resolves.
prompts.check: A final question of ten words or fewer naming a specific person, no answer given, and no paragraph ending on a resolution.

prompts.title: Page That Leaves A Gap
prompts.prompt: Write the last 200 words of a sales page for a service you sell. The outcome genuinely depends on what the client does after you leave.
prompts.constraint: You may not promise the outcome. The page closes on the condition that is not in your control, then the call to action, and nothing after it.
prompts.check: The closing names an uncontrolled condition, makes no outcome promise, and the call to action is the last element on the page.

prompts.title: Nine Days, No Ending
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about a practice that has not resolved into anything. There is nothing here you could report to anybody.
prompts.constraint: The word progress is banned from the whole essay. The last 100 words must introduce one new concrete fact and then stop. No paragraph may follow that fact.
prompts.check: The word progress is absent, a new concrete fact appears in the last 100 words, and the piece ends immediately after it.

prompts.title: The Page That Stays Open
prompts.prompt: Write a 400 word closing section for a page selling a service whose result depends on the client. Leave the ending unresolved and still ask for the click.
prompts.constraint: You may not promise the outcome. The last sentence before the button names the condition outside your control. No urgency, no scarcity, no summary of benefits.
prompts.check: No outcome promise anywhere, an uncontrolled condition in the final sentence, and the call to action still present.

prompts.title: Cut The Last Beat
prompts.prompt: Write 200 words about a fight with a friend. Then cut it to 150 by removing the ending you wanted to write.
prompts.constraint: Keep both versions. The final version ends at least two sentences earlier than your instinct wanted. List the removed sentences at the bottom.
prompts.check: Two or more sentences listed as removed, and the delivered piece ends on an unresolved beat.

prompts.title: A Piece That Refuses
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words about ambition. Arrive nowhere, on purpose, six separate times.
prompts.constraint: Six sections. Each ends unresolved. None may reference a previous section's ending. The final section may be neither the longest nor the shortest. No moral anywhere.
prompts.check: Six unresolved section endings, no cross-references between them, and a final section that is neither longest nor shortest.

prompts.title: Ten Endings, None Landing
prompts.prompt: Take one piece of about 140 words about a friendship that faded. Write ten different endings for it, none of which resolve anything.
prompts.constraint: Ten versions, each under 150 words. Every ending is a fact, an action, or an unanswered question. Banned in all ten: so, therefore, in the end, ultimately, lesson.
prompts.check: Ten versions with ten distinct unresolved endings, and zero banned words across the whole file.

prompts.title: The Question Never Asked
prompts.prompt: Write 1,000 words circling a question about your practice or your family. It has to be one you have never asked out loud.
prompts.constraint: The question appears once, as the final sentence, and is never answered or softened. Nothing follows it. No paragraph anywhere may end on a resolution.
prompts.check: The question appears exactly once as the last sentence, and no paragraph in the piece ends on a resolution.

prompts.title: Decline Without Hedging
prompts.prompt: Write five refusals of about twenty-five words each. Take the questions you actually get asked: your rates, your income, your beliefs, your process, your future.
