prompts.constraint: Each names the question precisely and declines it in one sentence. Banned: I do not know, maybe, perhaps, it depends, honestly. Each refusal gives a reason about the reader or the timing, never about your own ignorance.
prompts.check: Five precise questions, five one-sentence declines, zero hedging words, and no reason that admits you lack the answer.

prompts.title: What We Will Not Say
prompts.prompt: Write a 150 word section for a page selling your work. A real question about your method gets raised and then left unanswered.
prompts.constraint: Raise the question in the buyer's own words. Decline in one sentence. Give a reason that is about them, not about secrecy or ignorance. No teaser language and no learn more.
prompts.check: The question sits in buyer language, the decline gives a reader-centred reason, and no teaser phrasing appears.

prompts.title: The Thing I Will Not Write
prompts.prompt: Write 130 words that raise the most interesting question about your practice. Then refuse it and keep going.
prompts.constraint: Name the question exactly. Refuse it in under fifteen words. Then continue with something concrete for at least sixty words and never return to the question.
prompts.check: A specific question, a refusal under fifteen words, sixty or more words of concrete material after it, and no return.

prompts.title: Two Questions, One Answer
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about your pricing. Answer one obvious question fully and refuse a harder one.
prompts.constraint: The refused question must be more interesting than the answered one. The refusal is one sentence and does not apologise. Nothing in the essay may hint at the withheld answer.
prompts.check: One full answer, one apology-free single-sentence refusal, and no hint of the withheld answer anywhere in the file.

prompts.title: One Question, Left Standing
prompts.prompt: Write 450 words about your income and what people assume about it. End on one sentence that declines the question everybody asks you.
prompts.constraint: The refusal is the last sentence, runs under twelve words, and never claims you do not know. Give real figures about everything else in the entry.
prompts.check: A final sentence under twelve words that refuses cleanly, and at least three real figures elsewhere in the entry.

prompts.title: The Question We Skip
prompts.prompt: Write a 250 word FAQ block with four questions. Three get real answers and one gets a refusal.
prompts.constraint: The refused question sits third, not last. The refusal is two sentences maximum and must read as more confident than any of the three answers.
prompts.check: Four questions with the third refused in two sentences or fewer, and no hedging word inside the refusal.

prompts.title: What Happens After
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about death, or about what your practice is finally for. Refuse the central question three times in three different ways.
prompts.constraint: Three refusals: one because the reader is not ready, one because you are not, one because the question itself is wrong. None runs past two sentences. No sarcasm anywhere.
prompts.check: Three distinct refusals of two sentences or fewer, each with a different stated reason, and no sarcasm.

prompts.title: The Method We Withhold
prompts.prompt: Write a 400 word section for a page selling work you do. A real question about your method gets raised and refused, and the section still sells.
prompts.constraint: The question sits in the buyer's own words. The refusal is one sentence with a reason about them, never about secrecy. No teaser language and no learn more.
prompts.check: A buyer-worded question, a one-sentence refusal with a reader-centred reason, and zero teaser phrasing.

prompts.title: Six Refusals, Six Reasons
prompts.prompt: Write six refusals of about twenty-five words each. Cover work, money, family, health, practice, and the future.
prompts.constraint: Each raises a question a real person has asked you. Each declines with a reason. No reason may be reused. The word private may not appear.
prompts.check: Six questions, six distinct reasons, and zero uses of the word private.

prompts.title: The Essay That Withholds
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words about a formative experience. The central fact never gets stated on the page.
prompts.constraint: Everything around the fact must be exact. You may not use the words cannot, will not, or unable. The reader should finish able to say what happened without you having written it.
prompts.check: Search the file for the central fact. It appears nowhere, the three banned words are absent, and every scene around it carries at least two exact details.

prompts.title: Twelve Ways To Decline
prompts.prompt: Take the single question you are asked most and cannot answer. Write twelve refusals of about 100 words, each declining for a different reason.
prompts.constraint: Twelve versions, each under 150 words, with twelve different reasons and none repeated. Banned in all of them: I do not know, maybe, perhaps, it depends, honestly, private.
prompts.check: Twelve refusals with twelve distinct reasons, zero banned words, and no version admitting ignorance.

prompts.title: Ten Years From Now
prompts.prompt: Write 1,000 words about what you want your life to look like at thirty-one. Refuse to name the one thing you actually want.
prompts.constraint: Every other want is specified with a number or a place. The refusal is one clause, appears at roughly the two-thirds mark, and is never revisited.
prompts.check: Every named want carries a figure or a place, the refusal is one clause near two-thirds, and it never returns.

prompts.title: Say It For Them
prompts.prompt: Write five blocks of about thirty words each. Take the claims of yours that people doubt: your age, your rates, your results, your hours, your practice.
prompts.constraint: Each block opens by stating the doubt in the reader's own words, then declines to argue. Banned: trust me, I promise, believe me, I know it sounds.
prompts.check: Five blocks, five doubts in reader language, five explicit refusals to persuade, and zero banned phrases.

prompts.title: Pre-empt The Eye Roll
prompts.prompt: Write a 150 word section for a page whose main claim sounds inflated. The claim is true and the reader will still roll their eyes.
prompts.constraint: The first sentence is the reader's objection, phrased more harshly than they would phrase it. The second declines to convince them. Everything after gives facts and never argues.
prompts.check: The first sentence is the objection, the second refuses to persuade, and no sentence after that uses persuasive language.

prompts.title: You Will Not Believe This
prompts.prompt: Write 130 words about an experience in practice that sounds unbelievable. Write it for a skeptical friend who already thinks you have lost it.
prompts.constraint: Open with their disbelief. State plainly that you are not trying to convince them. Then report only what happened, with times and physical details.
prompts.check: Disbelief first, explicit non-persuasion second, and a remainder containing no argument and at least four physical details.

prompts.title: Not Here To Convince You
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about your daily practice. Your audience is designers who think it is superstition.
prompts.constraint: State the strongest version of their objection in the first 100 words. Refuse to argue in one sentence. Never mention the objection again. No defence anywhere in the piece.
prompts.check: The objection appears in the first 100 words in its strongest form, is refused once, and never reappears.

prompts.title: Written For A Cynic
prompts.prompt: Write 450 words about your practice for one friend who thinks you have lost it. Open in his voice, phrased sharper than he would put it.
prompts.constraint: The first forty words belong to him and contain no defence. Then one sentence declining to convince him. Everything after is facts with times and physical details.
prompts.check: Forty words of undefended objection, one non-persuasion sentence, and a remainder with no argument and at least six physical details.

prompts.title: Disqualify, Then Prove
prompts.prompt: Write a 300 word section for a service page. Name exactly why the reader thinks this will not work for them, then decline to talk them out of it.
prompts.constraint: Three doubts, each in the reader's own words. One refusal covering all three. Then evidence that never references the doubts again.
prompts.check: Three reader-voiced doubts, one refusal, and evidence that mentions none of the doubts.

prompts.title: The Claim I Cannot Prove
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words on something you believe from direct experience. You cannot evidence it to anybody and you are not going to try.
prompts.constraint: Voice the skeptic four times, each time immediately before making the point they would attack. Never rebut. State once, clearly, that you are not persuading anyone.
prompts.check: Four pre-emptive skeptic statements, zero rebuttals, and one clear non-persuasion sentence.

prompts.title: Page For The Unconvinced
prompts.prompt: Write a 400 word section for a page whose main claim sounds inflated even though it is true. Say the doubt out loud before the reader can.
prompts.constraint: Three doubts in the reader's own words, one refusal covering all three, then evidence that never references the doubts again. Banned: trust me, I promise, believe me.
prompts.check: Three reader-voiced doubts, one refusal to persuade, evidence mentioning none of the doubts, and zero banned phrases.

prompts.title: Nine Words Of Refusal
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words about a result you got that people assume is fake. Give them the numbers and nothing else.
prompts.constraint: The doubt takes forty words in the reader's voice. Your refusal to persuade is nine words or fewer. The remaining words are numbers, dates, and names only.
prompts.check: A forty word doubt, a refusal of nine words or fewer, and a remainder made only of verifiable detail.

prompts.title: Writing For A Hostile Reader
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words on a strong opinion you hold about design work. Your reader thinks you are too young to hold it.
prompts.constraint: Six pre-emptions, each stating the reader's objection before you make the claim. No rebuttal at any point. One refusal to persuade, placed in the final third.
prompts.check: Six pre-emptions, zero rebuttals, and a single non-persuasion sentence inside the last 400 words.

prompts.title: Ten Doubts, Ten Openers
prompts.prompt: Write ten opening blocks of about 120 words each for a page aimed at buyers burned by three agencies. Each opens on a different scar, in their words.
prompts.constraint: Ten versions, each under 150 words. Each states the doubt more harshly than the reader would, then declines to argue. No version may defend anything.
prompts.check: Ten versions with ten distinct reader-voiced scars, ten refusals to persuade, and zero defensive sentences.

prompts.title: Letter To Sixteen
prompts.prompt: Write 1,000 words to your sixteen-year-old self. He would find all of this ridiculous and he would say so.
prompts.constraint: He objects at least eight times in his own words and you never argue him down. You may only report what happened. State once that you are not trying to convince him.
prompts.check: Eight objections in his voice, zero counterarguments, and one explicit non-persuasion line.

prompts.title: Last, Shortest, Unsignalled
prompts.prompt: Write five paragraphs of about forty words each about your own work habits. Each one ends on a joke.
prompts.constraint: The joke is the last sentence and the shortest sentence in its paragraph. No signalling: no ha, no lol, no obviously, no of course, no italics. The target is always you.
prompts.check: Five paragraphs where the final sentence is the shortest by word count, and every joke targets you.

prompts.title: One Joke, No Wink
prompts.prompt: Write four copy blocks of about fifty words for a service page. Each one ends on a dry line at your own expense.
prompts.constraint: The joke is last and shortest. No exclamation marks, no emoji, no rhetorical questions. The reader is never the target and neither is the client.
prompts.check: Four blocks, four shortest-last sentences, no punctuation doing the signalling, and no joke aimed at a buyer.

prompts.title: Laugh At The Sitter
prompts.prompt: Write 130 words about your own meditation. Put three jokes in it, all of them about you.
prompts.constraint: Three paragraphs, one joke each, always last and always shortest. Nothing about the practice itself may be the joke. Never mock a teacher or a tradition.
prompts.check: Three paragraphs, three shortest-last jokes, and every target is you.

prompts.title: The Expert And Me
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about advice from design experts. None of it survived contact with a real client.
prompts.constraint: Six paragraphs end on a joke. Three target you and three target the expert. Every joke is the shortest sentence in its paragraph and none of them is set up in advance.
prompts.check: Six jokes, three self-targeted and three expert-targeted, each the shortest sentence in its paragraph.

prompts.title: Noon, Written Funny
prompts.prompt: Write 450 words about waking at noon and what the rest of the house has already finished doing. Make it funny without ever announcing it.
prompts.constraint: Six paragraphs, each ending on the shortest sentence in that paragraph. No signalling and no set-up lines. Nobody at home may be the target.
prompts.check: Six paragraphs with shortest-last endings, zero set-up sentences, and no joke aimed at a family member.

prompts.title: Dry About Ourselves
prompts.prompt: Write a 250 word about section for your agency page. It has to be funny at your own expense and still sell.
prompts.constraint: Three jokes maximum, each the last and shortest sentence in its paragraph. No joke may undercut the competence claim made in the same paragraph.
prompts.check: Three jokes in the required position, and every paragraph still makes one competence claim that survives its joke.

prompts.title: Family Comedy, No Butt
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about how your family sees your work. Keep it funny throughout with nobody in the family as the butt of anything.
prompts.constraint: Eight jokes, all targeting you or the profession. Each is last and shortest in its paragraph. No family member may be the target of any joke.
prompts.check: Eight jokes in position, zero targeting a family member, and each the shortest sentence in its paragraph.

prompts.title: Funny Enough To Sell
prompts.prompt: Write a 400 word section for a service page that is funny at your own expense and still closes. The industry can take a hit and the buyer never can.
prompts.constraint: Four jokes, each the last and shortest sentence in its paragraph. None within fifty words of a price. Every paragraph keeps one competence claim intact.
prompts.check: Four shortest-last jokes, none near a price, and four competence claims that survive their jokes.

prompts.title: Five Words Or Fewer
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words about a client call that went badly. Put three jokes in it, none longer than five words.
prompts.constraint: Each joke is five words or fewer, sits last in its paragraph, and is the shortest sentence there. No joke may be about the client.
prompts.check: Three jokes of five words or fewer, all last in their paragraphs, and none targeting the client.

prompts.title: Funny About Money
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words about money at twenty-one. Make a reader laugh eight times and never feel laughed at.
prompts.constraint: Ten jokes. Eight target you and two target the industry. All are last and shortest in their paragraphs. No joke may touch poverty, caste, or anybody's family.
prompts.check: Ten jokes in position with the required targets, and none touching the three banned subjects.

prompts.title: One Humiliation, Twelve Cuts
prompts.prompt: Take one embarrassing thing that happened to you this year. Write it twelve times at about 120 words, each version ending on a different joke.
prompts.constraint: Twelve versions, each under 150 words. Twelve different closing jokes, each five words or fewer and the shortest sentence in its version. You are the target every time.
prompts.check: Twelve versions with twelve distinct closing jokes of five words or fewer, each the shortest sentence there, all self-targeted.

prompts.title: A Year Of Small Humiliations
prompts.prompt: Write 1,000 words about this year's embarrassments. Give each one its own section.
prompts.constraint: Twelve jokes, one per section, all at your own expense. No section may explain why the joke is funny. Each joke is the shortest sentence in its section.
prompts.check: Twelve jokes, one per section, each the shortest sentence there, and zero explanations attached.

prompts.title: Count Every Sentence
prompts.prompt: Write 140 words about the last hour before you sleep. Then count the words in every sentence and post the sequence at the bottom.
prompts.constraint: The sequence must alternate between above twenty and below eight, with no two consecutive sentences on the same side. Minimum eight sentences.
prompts.check: The posted sequence alternates strictly between twenty-plus and under-eight across at least eight sentences.

prompts.title: Long, Long, Short
prompts.prompt: Write four copy blocks of about sixty words each for a service you sell. All four run on a strict rhythm you never break.
prompts.constraint: Every block runs long, long, short, where long is twenty-two words or more and short is six words or fewer. Post the counts under each block.
prompts.check: Four blocks, each with two sentences of twenty-two or more and one of six or fewer, in that order, with counts shown.

prompts.title: Three, Two, One
prompts.prompt: Write 130 words about the walk from your room to the kitchen at 2am. Everybody else is asleep.
prompts.constraint: Sentence lengths descend in every group of three: long, medium, short, repeated. Long is over twenty words, medium is ten to fifteen, short is under seven.
prompts.check: Every group of three sentences descends through the three bands, with counts posted at the bottom.

prompts.title: Write The Score First
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words about a project you rebuilt three times. Compose the sentence lengths before you write a single word.
prompts.constraint: Write the length score first as a list of numbers, then write the essay to match within two words per sentence. Post the score above the essay.
prompts.check: Every sentence in the essay lands within two words of the corresponding number in the posted score.

prompts.title: The One Short Sentence
prompts.prompt: Write 450 words about the moment a client said yes to your highest ever quote. One sentence in the entry does all the work.
prompts.constraint: Every sentence runs eighteen to twenty-five words except one, which is three words or fewer and lands at the turn. No other short sentence anywhere.
prompts.check: One sentence of three words or fewer sitting at the turn, with every other sentence between eighteen and twenty-five words.

prompts.title: Cadence For The Ask
prompts.prompt: Write three closing sections of about eighty words each. Each has a different rhythm and all three lead to the same call to action.
prompts.constraint: Version one accelerates, with every sentence shorter than the last. Version two holds steady at twelve to fifteen words. Version three alternates twenty-five and five. Post counts for all three.
prompts.check: Three versions matching the three specified patterns exactly, with the counts posted.

prompts.title: Long Breath, Short Breath
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about a week of illness. Sentence length alone has to carry the fever.
prompts.constraint: The first third averages twenty-four words per sentence, the middle third averages nine, the last third averages sixteen. Each third must land within one word of its target.
prompts.check: Compute the average sentence length of each third. All three land within one word of twenty-four, nine, and sixteen.

prompts.title: Cadence Built To Convert
prompts.prompt: Write a 400 word page section where the rhythm does the persuading. Compose the sentence lengths before you write a single word of it.
prompts.constraint: Post the length score above the section. It must contain at least two sentences over thirty-five words and at least six under five. Match it within two words per sentence.
prompts.check: A posted score meeting both counts, and every written sentence within two words of its scored length.

prompts.title: One Long, Nine Short
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words about the second you realised a file was lost. One sentence holds the whole panic and the rest hold nothing.
prompts.constraint: One sentence of sixty words or more. Nine sentences of six words or fewer. Nothing in between. The long one may not be first or last.
prompts.check: Exactly ten sentences: one over sixty words in a middle position, and nine under seven.

prompts.title: Composed Rhythm, Twelve Hundred
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words about your relationship with work. Score the rhythm before you write a word of it.
prompts.constraint: Write a length score for every sentence first. It must contain at least four sentences over forty words and at least fifteen under five. Match the score within three words per sentence.
prompts.check: The score meets both counts, and every written sentence lands within three words of its scored length.

prompts.title: Same Words, Eight Rhythms
prompts.prompt: Take one 140 word piece about the second you realised a file was lost. Rewrite it eight times, keeping every fact and changing only the sentence lengths.
prompts.constraint: Eight versions, each under 150 words, each with a different length pattern posted underneath as a list of counts. No fact may be added or dropped between versions.
prompts.check: Eight versions carrying identical facts, eight posted count sequences, and no two sequences alike.

prompts.title: The Longest Sentence
prompts.prompt: Write 1,000 words about a single whole day. One sentence in it runs to at least 150 words and never uses a semicolon.
prompts.constraint: One sentence of 150 words or more with no semicolon and no more than eight commas. Every other sentence in the piece runs under twelve words.
prompts.check: One sentence of 150-plus words with eight commas or fewer and no semicolon, and every other sentence under twelve words.

prompts.title: One Line For Logistics
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words about a client project from the first message to the launch. Only one moment gets shown in full.
prompts.constraint: All travel, scheduling, emails, invoices, and file transfers compress into a single reported sentence. Exactly one scene may be dramatised and it must be the one where somebody changed their mind.
prompts.check: One dramatised scene, one logistics sentence covering everything else, and no second scene.

prompts.title: Case Study In 150
prompts.prompt: Compress a real six week project into 150 words of case study. Everything except one moment gets reported rather than shown.
prompts.constraint: One sentence for the whole process. One scene for the moment the client understood something. One line for the result with a number. Nothing else.
prompts.check: Three parts only, in that order, with the process at one sentence and the result carrying a figure.

prompts.title: Skip The Getting There
prompts.prompt: Write 130 words about a family function you had to attend. You lost most of a working day to it.
prompts.constraint: Everything before you arrived is one sentence. Everything after you left is banned. Only one exchange may be shown in full.
prompts.check: One sentence covers the arrival logistics, no material after your departure appears, and exactly one exchange is dramatised.

prompts.title: Three Scenes, One Year
prompts.prompt: Write 700 words covering a year of work. You get three scenes and nothing more.
prompts.constraint: Three dramatised moments, each one where a person changes. Everything between them is reported in one sentence per gap, two gaps maximum. No scene may exceed 180 words.
prompts.check: Three scenes, two single-sentence gaps, and every scene containing a person changing their mind or their behaviour.

prompts.title: Half The Words, Same Facts
prompts.prompt: Take a 500 word entry you wrote this week and cut it to 250. Nothing factual may be lost on the way.
prompts.constraint: Every cut comes from logistics, transitions, or restated feeling. No fact, number, name, or line of speech may go. Post both versions.
prompts.check: Both versions posted, the second at 250 words or fewer, and every fact from the first still present in the second.

prompts.title: Long Story, Short Section
prompts.prompt: Write a 200 word origin section for your agency page. It has to cover three years.
prompts.constraint: One scene only. Everything else is two reported sentences. No list of dates in sequence, no we started as, no journey language.
prompts.check: One scene, two reported sentences of history, and no chronological list anywhere.

prompts.title: Where Somebody Changes
prompts.prompt: Write 900 words about your first year in business. Dramatise only the four moments where somebody changed.
prompts.constraint: Four scenes. Everything else, including all money movement and all tooling, is reported in four sentences total. Mark each scene with the name of who changed.
prompts.check: Four scenes, four marked names, and four or fewer sentences carrying all the remaining material.

prompts.title: Eight Months, Three Scenes
prompts.prompt: Write a 400 word case study section covering an eight month engagement. Only three moments get shown in full.
prompts.constraint: Three scenes, each one where somebody changes. All process, onboarding, calls, and revisions compress to one sentence each. The result carries three numbers.
prompts.check: Three scenes with a person changing in each, three process sentences in total, and three figures in the result.

prompts.title: Three Sentences Of Logistics
prompts.prompt: Write 150 words about a trip to a client's office in another city. The whole day took eleven hours and one of them mattered.
prompts.constraint: The travel, the waiting, the security desk, and the return take three sentences in total. The meeting is one scene. That scene must contain one line of speech that changed the deal.
prompts.check: Three logistics sentences, one scene, and one quoted line that visibly changes the outcome.

prompts.title: A Decade In Twelve Hundred
prompts.prompt: Write 1,200 words about ten years, from eleven years old to twenty-one. Six scenes carry all of it.
prompts.constraint: Six scenes maximum. Every scene features a person changing. All other years compress into six reported sentences, one per gap. No sentence may list more than three facts.
prompts.check: Six scenes, six gap sentences, and no sentence containing more than three facts.

prompts.title: One Project, Ten Compressions
prompts.prompt: Take one real six week project. Write it ten times at about 140 words, each version dramatising a different single moment.
prompts.constraint: Ten versions, each under 150 words. Each shows exactly one scene and reports everything else in one sentence. No two versions may dramatise the same moment.
prompts.check: Ten versions with ten different dramatised moments, and one reported logistics sentence in each.

prompts.title: The Year, Cut Down
prompts.prompt: Write 1,000 words about the past year. Nothing gets described unless somebody changed.
prompts.constraint: Five scenes. Everything else is reported. All the reported material together must run under 150 words. No scene may be about you alone.
prompts.check: Five scenes each involving a second person changing, and all reported material summing to under 150 words.
